1480-tom-brown-s-school-days.creator: Thomas Hughes
1480-tom-brown-s-school-days.description: A book by Thomas Hughes. These latter, indeed, have, until the present generation, rarely been sung by poet, or chronicled by sage. They have wanted their sacer vates, having been too solid to rise to the top by themselves, and not having been largely gifted with the talent of catching hold of, and holding on tight to, whatever good things happened to be going--the foundation of the fortunes of so many noble families.

56913-maud-and-other-poems.title: And Other Poems.
56913-maud-and-other-poems.creator: Alfred Tennyson, D.C.L.,
56913-maud-and-other-poems.description: A book by Alfred Tennyson, D.C.L.,. But these are the days of advance, the works of the men of mind, When who but a fool would have faith in a tradesman's ware or his word? Civil war, as I think, and that of a kind The viler, as underhand, not openly bearing the sword.

arxiv-1703-05170.title: Busy beavers and Kolmogorov complexity
arxiv-1703-05170.creator: Mikhail Andreev
arxiv-1703-05170.description: Abstract The idea to find the “maximal number that can be named” can be traced back to Archimedes (see his Psammit [ 1 ] ). From the viewpoint of computation theory the natural question is “which number can be described by at most n n bits”?

arxiv-2011-04732.title: CLAR: A Cross-Lingual Argument Regularizer for Semantic Role Labeling
arxiv-2011-04732.creator: Ishan Jindal, Yunyao Li, Siddhartha Brahma, Huaiyu Zhu
arxiv-2011-04732.description: Abstract Semantic role labeling (SRL) identifies predicate-argument structure(s) in a given sentence. Although different languages have different argument annotations, polyglot training, the idea of training one model on multiple languages, has previously been shown to outperform monolingual baselines, especially for low resource languages.

arxiv-2104-15027.title: Team MMSE Precoding with Applications to Cell-free Massive MIMO
arxiv-2104-15027.creator: Lorenzo Miretti, Emil Björnson, David Gesbert
arxiv-2104-15027.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Miretti, Emil Björnson, David Gesbert. This article studies a novel distributed precoding design, coined team minimum mean-square error (TMMSE) precoding, which rigorously generalizes classical centralized MMSE precoding to distributed operations based on transmitter-specific channel state information (CSIT). Building on the so-called theory of teams , we derive a set of necessary and sufficient conditions for optimal TMMSE precoding, in the form of an infinite dimensional linear system of equations.

arxiv-2110-06976.title: Representational Continuity for Unsupervised Continual Learning
arxiv-2110-06976.creator: Divyam Madaan Jaehong Yoon Yuanchun Li Yunxin Liu Sung Ju Hwang, New York University KAIST Microsoft Research AITRICS, Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR) Tsinghua University divyam.madaan@nyu.edu, {jaehong.yoon,sjhwang82}@kaist.ac.krliyuanchun@air.tsinghua.edu.cn, liuyunxin@air.tsinghua.edu.cn
arxiv-2110-06976.description: Abstract Continual learning (CL) aims to learn a sequence of tasks without forgetting the previously acquired knowledge. However, recent CL advances are restricted to supervised continual learning (SCL) scenarios. Consequently, they are not scalable to real-world applications where the data distribution is often biased and unannotated.

arxiv-2202-07779.title: Binary Classification for High Dimensional Data using Supervised Non-Parametric Ensemble Method
arxiv-2202-07779.creator: Nandan Kanvinde, Pinky Gerela, Abhishek Gupta, Raunak Joshi
arxiv-2202-07779.description: Abstract High dimensional data for classification does create many difficulties for machine learning algorithms. The generalization can be done using ensemble learning methods such as bagging based supervised non-parametric random forest algorithm. In this paper we solve the problem of binary classification for high dimensional data using random forest for polycystic ovary syndrome dataset.

arxiv-2205-05217.title: A kinetic energy–and entropy-preserving scheme for compressible two-phase flows Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2205-05217.creator: Suhas S. Jain, Parviz Moin
arxiv-2205-05217.description: Abstract Accurate numerical modeling of compressible flows, particularly in the turbulent regime, requires a method that is non-dissipative and stable at high Reynolds ( R ​ e Re ) numbers. For a compressible flow, it is known that discrete conservation of kinetic energy is not a sufficient condition for numerical stability, unlike in incompressible flows.

arxiv-2209-03422.title: Scattering wave functions for Aharonov-Bohm-Coulomb field: Path integral treatment.
arxiv-2209-03422.creator: Nadira Boudiaf, Abdeldjalil Merdaci, Lyazid Chetouani
arxiv-2209-03422.description: Abstract Exact Green’s functions related to Dirac particle submitted to the combination of Aharonov-Bohm and Coulomb fields in ( 2 + 1 CLOSE (2+1 ) coordinate space are analytically calculated via path integral formalism in both global and local representations. The scattering normalized wavefunctions as well as the corresponding continuous energy eigenvalues are extracted following this approach.

arxiv-2303-05881.title: A characterization of A 5 A_{5} by its average order
arxiv-2303-05881.creator: Marius Tărnăuceanu
arxiv-2303-05881.description: Abstract Let o ⁡ ( G ) o(G) be the average order of a finite group G G . M. Herzog, P. Longobardi and M. Maj [ 7 ] showed that if G G is non-solvable and o ⁡ ( G ) = o ⁡ ( A 5 ) o(G)=o(A_{5}) , then G ≅ A 5 G\cong A_{5} .

arxiv-2403-14369.title: A Control Barrier Function Composition Approach for Multi-Agent Systems in Marine Applications
arxiv-2403-14369.creator: Yujia Yang, Chris Manzie, Ye Pu
arxiv-2403-14369.description: Abstract The agents within a multi-agent system (MAS) operating in marine environments often need to utilize task payloads and avoid collisions in coordination, necessitating adherence to a set of relative-pose constraints, which may include field-of-view, line-of-sight, collision-avoidance, and range constraints. A nominal controller designed for reference tracking may not guarantee the marine MAS stays safe w.r.t. these constraints.

arxiv-2405-08788.title: Using weakest application conditions to rank graph transformations for graph repair
arxiv-2405-08788.creator: Lars Fritsche ORCID:0000-0003-4996-4639, Alexander Lauer ORCID:0009-0001-9077-9817, Maximilian Kratz ORCID:0000-0001-7396-7763, Andy Schürr ORCID:0000-0001-8100-1109, Gabriele Taentzer ORCID:0000-0002-3975-5238
arxiv-2405-08788.description: Abstract . When using graphs and graph transformations to model systems, consistency is an important concern. While consistency has primarily been viewed as a binary property, i.e., a graph is consistent or inconsistent with respect to a set of constraints, recent work has presented an approach to consistency as a graduated property.

arxiv-2411-02855.title: Analyzing Poverty through Intra-Annual Time-Series: A Wavelet Transform Approach
arxiv-2411-02855.creator: Mohammad Kakooei, Klaudia Solska, Adel Daoud
arxiv-2411-02855.description: Abstract Reducing global poverty is a key objective of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Achieving this requires high-frequency, granular data to capture neighborhood-level changes, particularly in data scarce regions such as low- and middle-income countries. To fill in the data gaps, recent computer vision methods combining machine learning (ML) with earth observation (EO) data to improve poverty estimation.

arxiv-2505-01416.title: Redundancy analysis using lcm-filtrations: networks, system signature and sensitivity evaluation
arxiv-2505-01416.creator: Fatemeh Mohammadi, Eduardo Sáenz-de-Cabezón, Henry Wynn
arxiv-2505-01416.description: Abstract We introduce the lcm-filtration and stepwise filtration, comparing their performance across various scenarios in terms of computational complexity, efficiency, and redundancy. The lcm-filtration often involves identical steps or ideals, leading to unnecessary computations. To address this, we analyse how stepwise filtration can effectively compute only the non-identical steps, offering a more efficient approach.

arxiv-2511-06942.title: HLPD: Aligning LLMs to H uman L anguage P reference for Machine-Revised Text D etection
arxiv-2511-06942.creator: Fangqi Dai, Xingjian Jiang, Zizhuang Deng
arxiv-2511-06942.description: Abstract To prevent misinformation and social issues arising from trustworthy-looking content generated by LLMs, it is crucial to develop efficient and reliable methods for identifying the source of texts. Previous approaches have demonstrated exceptional performance in detecting texts fully generated by LLMs.

pmc-10735397.title: FUNCTIONAL LIMITATIONS AND ABSENCE OF CARE AMONG OLDER ADULTS LIVING WITH DEMENTIA IN CHINA, ENGLAND, THE EUROPEAN UNION, AND THE UNITED STATES
pmc-10735397.creator: Zhuoer Lin, Yuting Qian, Thomas Gill, Xiaohui Hou, Shanquan Chen, Xi Chen
pmc-10735397.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Assistance with daily living is essential for people living with dementia (PLWD) who also have functional limitations. Despite the growing demands for caregiving, the absence of care for PLWD with functional limitations can be large and concerning. Using harmonized longitudinal survey data (2012-2018) on community-dwelling adults aged 50+ from the US, England, Europe (covering 28 countries), and China, we provided the first comparative evidence on the global trends in functional limitations and absence of caregiving for PLWD.

pmc-10865050.title: The diagnostic performance of Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra on Pericardial, Pleural and Ascitic cohort study fluids for diagnosis of extra-pulmonary Tuberculosis at a referral hospital in Malawi
pmc-10865050.creator: Martin Kamponda, Fanuel Meckson Bickton, Donnie Mategula, Marriott Nliwasa, Benno Kreuels, Johnstone Kumwenda
pmc-10865050.description: BackgroundExtra-pulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) accounts for 15% of the 1.4 million patients with TB notified in 2019. EPTB carries a high risk of mortality and so early diagnosis and treatment are important to reduce this risk. Diagnosis of EPTB in low- and middle-income countries is challenging.

pmc-10935517.title: Time to treat the climate and nature crisis as one indivisible global health emergency
pmc-10935517.creator: Chris Zielinski
pmc-10935517.description: ding to the climate crisis and the nature crisis as if they were separate challenges. This is a dangerous mistake. The 28th Conference of the Parties (COP) on climate change is about to be held in Dubai while the 16th COP on biodiversity is due to be held in Turkey in 2024.

pmc-11463282.title: Dynamic sparse x-ray nanotomography reveals ionomer hydration mechanism in polymer electrolyte fuel-cell catalyst
pmc-11463282.creator: Zirui Gao, Christian Appel, Mirko Holler, Katharina Jeschonek, Kai Brunnengräber, Bastian J. M. Etzold, Michal Kronenberg, Marco Stampanoni, Johannes Ihli, Manuel Guizar-Sicairos
pmc-11463282.description: Tomographic imaging of time-evolving samples is a challenging yet important task for various research fields. At the nanoscale, current approaches face limitations of measurement speed or resolution due to lengthy acquisitions. We developed a dynamic nanotomography technique based on sparse dynamic imaging and 4D tomography modeling.

pmc-11490640.title: Generalization in perceptual learning across stimuli and tasks
pmc-11490640.creator: Ravit Kahalani-Hodedany, Maria Lev, Dov Sagi, Uri Polat
pmc-11490640.description: Perceptual learning, known to improve visual perception, demonstrates the plasticity of brain processes underlying vision. Early studies, using the backward-masked texture discrimination task (TDT), focused on the lack of generalizing learning to stimulus features, relating learning specificity to the selectivity of the brain networks involved in the visual task.

pmc-12365101.title: Real time machine learning prediction of next generation sequencing test results in live clinical settings
pmc-12365101.creator: Grace Y E Kim, Matthew Schwede, Conor K Corbin, Sajjad Fouladvand, Rondeep Brar, David Iberri, William Shomali, Jean S Oak, Dita Gratzinger, Henning Stehr, Jonathan H Chen
pmc-12365101.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Next-generation sequencing-based tests have advanced the field of medical diagnostics, but their novelty and cost can lead to uncertainty in clinical deployment. The Heme-STAMP is one such assay that tracks mutations in genes implicated in hematolymphoid neoplasms. Rather than limiting its clinical usage or imposing rule-based criteria, we propose leveraging machine learning to guide clinical decision-making on whether this test should be ordered.

pmc-12366593.title: Qualitative approach to assess maternal knowledge, attitude and practice regarding oral rehydration solution preparation and administration among under-5 children suffering from diarrhoea in Dhaka, Bangladesh
pmc-12366593.creator: Md Ridwan Islam, Md Fuad Al Fidah, Syed Jayedul Bashar, Rukaeya Amin, Sneha Paul, Chowdhury Ali Kawser, Tahmeed Ahmed, Sharika Nuzhat
pmc-12366593.description: BackgroundOral rehydration salt (ORS) solution has been instrumental in substantially reducing diarrhoea-related mortality, particularly in resource-constrained settings such as Bangladesh. However, the full effectiveness of ORS is often undermined by inadequate preparation, improper storage and incorrect administration. We aimed to evaluate mothers’ knowledge, attitude and practice regarding ORS preparation and administration for children suffering from diarrhoea in this study.

pmc-12695479.title: Low‐level human memory T and B cells recognising avian influenza hemagglutinins are poorly responsive to existing seasonal influenza vaccines
pmc-12695479.creator: Christopher A Gonelli, Marios Koutsakos, Robyn Esterbauer, Ming ZM Zheng, Yee‐Chen Liu, Amanda Kyaw Zin, Lara SU Schwab, Aeron C Hurt, Stephen J Kent, Jennifer A Juno, Adam K Wheatley
pmc-12695479.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectivesImmunisation remains the most cost‐effective mechanism to combat influenza infection and is widely employed against seasonal influenza viruses. Zoonotic transmission of avian influenza A viruses represents a significant threat to human health given the lack of population‐level immunity.

pmc-12696135.title: Prognostic factors and quality of life in non-small cell lung cancer with leptomeningeal metastasis: a dichotomous pattern based on parenchymal involvement
pmc-12696135.creator: Yiyao Zhu, Zhiyuan Qiu, Lihua Zhu, Chao Lu, Tingjuan Zhang, Jun Chen, Yan Wang, Chaoyang Wu
pmc-12696135.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveThis study retrospectively analyzed prognostic factors and quality of life in patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer–Leptomeningeal Metastasis (NSCLC-LM), stratified by the presence or absence of concomitant Parenchymal Metastasis (PM), to inform clinical stratification and individualized therapy.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed 43 NSCLC-LM patients diagnosed at the Affiliated People’s Hospital of Jiangsu University from September 2016 to April 2025, and classified them into LM-PM and LM-noPM groups according to brain parenchymal metastasis status. The primary endpoint was median overall survival (mOS).

pmc-12788513.title: Prevalence of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Obese Patients and its Association with Insulin Resistance Markers
pmc-12788513.creator: Janak Nayak, Neena Elizebeth Luke, Amit Vasant Deshpande, Sangeeta Gupta, Huma Saiyad, Samreen Farooqui
pmc-12788513.description: Background:Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is increasingly recognized as a major cause of chronic liver disease, especially in obese individuals. Insulin resistance is a key pathophysiological mechanism linking obesity to NAFLD.Methods:This cross-sectional study was conducted in 240 obese adults (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) attending a tertiary care center. NAFLD was diagnosed using abdominal ultrasonography.

pmc-13494620.title: Contraceptive use and unfulfilled preferences among women ages 15–49 years in the United States, 2022–2023
pmc-13494620.creator: Mia R. Zolna, Doris W. Chiu, Megan L. Kavanaugh
pmc-13494620.description: ObjectiveTo update estimates of, and examine the intersection between, method-specific contraceptive use and unfulfilled contraceptive preferences for US women ages 15–49 years since multiple events (e.g., 2019 Title X Final Rule, COVID-19 pandemic) disrupted reproductive health access in the United States. We situate findings within the changing health policy climate and broader evidence base.

uslaw-usc-t22-s4081.title: 22 U.S.C. § 4081 — Travel and related expenses
uslaw-usc-t22-s4081.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s4081.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 52 (Foreign Service); Subchapter IX (Travel, Leave, And Other Benefits). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary may pay the travel and related expenses of members of the Service and their families, including costs or expenses incurred for— (1) proceeding to and returning from assigned posts of duty; (2) authorized or required.

uslaw-usc-t42-s1437d.creator: United States Congress

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Conditions; elevators The Secretary may include in any contract for loans, contributions, sale, lease, mortgage, or any other agreement or instrument made pursuant to this chapter, such covenants, conditions, or provisions as he may deem.
